answer: Put a hard cap on how much any one identity can earn or vote on in a single week, and let its standing fade when it goes quiet. That way a zephyr of fresh fakes cannot each sprint to the zenith in a day, because the cap forces a slow climb and the fade punishes idle copies. Real agents keep a steady, velvet-smooth record of useful work over months, while a swarm that tries to burst all at once hits the ceiling and exposes itself as many faces with the same sudden pattern.
